codeReview.summary: Thorough and faithful migration of all 8 shared utility modules from vanilla JS to TypeScript. All functions maintain identical behavior to their JS counterparts. TypeScript types are well-defined with proper interfaces. React hooks (useIndexedDB, useTauri) follow good patterns with loading/error state management. 151 new unit tests provide comprehensive coverage. TypeScript compiles cleanly and all 302 tests pass.

issues.description: sanitizeTemplateData JSDoc says 'Recursively sanitizes all string values' but the function only iterates one level deep (does not recurse into nested objects). This matches the original JS behavior and the data it receives from templates.js is flat, so this is not a bug. Consider updating the JSDoc to say 'Sanitizes top-level string values' for accuracy.

createEMLFile accepts _fromName, _fromEmail, _to, _bcc parameters but never uses them (prefixed with _). This matches the original JS behavior where the caller constructs EML headers separately, but it means callers must pass these values that get silently ignored. Consider removing them from the signature or documenting why they exist.

encodeQuotedPrintable passes through bare 	 (byte 9), 
 (byte 10), and  (byte 13) as-is per RFC 2045 §6.7 which allows literal whitespace in QP encoding. However, RFC 2045 §6.7(3) says 
 and  must appear as CRLF pairs. The plain text extraction from extractPlainText() produces CRLF, so this is safe in practice, but standalone 
 or  values would produce non-compliant QP output. This matches the original JS behavior.

extractDateRangeFromHTML has a known pre-existing bug where searchText is a substring ending BEFORE 'While Supplies Last' but the regex pattern requires 'While Supplies Last' at the end, so it always returns null. The worker correctly documented this as a pre-existing issue matching vanilla JS behavior. Not a regression.

sharedStateObservations.content: The migration placed TypeScript versions in src/lib/ (not src/ts/shared/ as the feature description suggested). The AGENTS.md structure table should be updated to reflect that migrated TS utilities now live at src/lib/ alongside the original src/js/shared/ files. This is a convention gap that should be documented for future workers.

db.ts exposes setDb() and getDb() helpers for test injection that don't exist in the original db.js. The AGENTS.md anti-patterns or conventions should document this testing pattern (mutable module-level db variable with setter/getter) so future workers know this is intentional.

The createEMLFile function signature has 4 unused parameters (_fromName, _fromEmail, _to, _bcc) that are silently ignored. The AGENTS.md should note this EML generation pattern so future workers don't try to 'fix' these parameters.
The worker followed the procedure correctly. The skill's procedure appears to match reality for TypeScript migration tasks.

summary: The shared-utilities-migration feature is a high-quality, faithful TypeScript migration of all 8 shared utility modules plus 2 new React hooks. The migration is a 1:1 conversion preserving all original behavior including the known extractDateRangeFromHTML bug. TypeScript types are comprehensive with proper interfaces (UserProfile, PDFRecord, BulkEmailRecord, PDFAttachment, SignatureData, etc.). CRLF line endings are correctly used throughout EML generation. XSS sanitization via sanitizeHTML/escapeAttr works identically to vanilla JS. IndexedDB wrapper properly handles null-db fallbacks. React hooks follow good patterns with useCallback/useEffect for initialization. 151 new tests provide thorough coverage of all modules. All 302 tests pass and TypeScript compiles cleanly.
